rationale: All 28 spec criteria pass (acceptance lens clean). One defensive-coding gap survives triage: fetchToolConfigs guards against non-array response, empty entry objects, and null configVal — but not against a null/undefined element in the array itself. Object.entries(null) throws, the outer catch fires, and all defaults accumulated before that element are discarded. The fix is a one-line null guard consistent with the existing defensive pattern. Fallbacks work in this scenario so user-visible impact is limited, but the omission is inconsistent with the surrounding defensive code. Seven findings dismissed (xrayconfig fixture concern invalid — actual file uses base_url correctly; githubconfig intentionally excluded; fire-and-forget timing by design; empty-string filter per spec; entries[0] per API contract; getDefaultUrl deletion per spec; github/gitlab collision speculative). Three findings deferred as pre-existing behaviour not introduced by this PR (no-logging in catch, template-token fallback strings, http-scheme fallback strings).

findings.title: fetchToolConfigs: null/undefined array element causes TypeError and discards accumulated defaults
findings.problem: The for-of loop calls Object.entries(entry) on each array element. If an element is null or undefined, Object.entries throws a TypeError. The outer catch fires, leaving toolUrlDefaults as {} and discarding any defaults accumulated before the null element in that loop run.
findings.impact: All configured URL defaults are silently lost for that app startup. Users see hardcoded fallback URLs instead of deployment-configured ones. No crash or data loss, but the feature's core value is negated silently when a null element appears before valid entries.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line null guard at the top of the loop body: if (entry == null) continue — consistent with the existing guards for empty entries, null configVal, and non-array response.
